chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Jimmy Blyth, Tiny Parham and the Apollo Theatre as a training ground
summary: As a peanut boy at the Apollo on 47th Street he met pianists Blyth and Parham and played snare quietly beside them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Right, right, he was with Jimmy Blyth on -- right, right, right.

Right, I remember. See, I was coming in -- I mean, I was coming in, and these guys were getting ready to go out, you know? And this was the thing. But I got a chance -- Jimmy Blyth was selling peanuts and popcorn at the Apollo Theatre on 47th Street. And they used to have -- they couldn't have a band, so they had piano players. And Jimmy Blyth used to play the pictures there. And then Tiny Parham played the pictures there.
So I got a chance to meet him and talk with him,

and then I used to listen to his records and all of that. But I was just the peanut and popcorn boy at that time. And then I would go and get a drum, it was just a snare drum, that's all I had, and then they would let me sit down there with them and play. Say, keep quiet, play quiet. No, that was my training grounds.
